title: Exponents and scientific notation
lede: Repeated multiplication, the exponent rules, and how scientists write huge and tiny numbers.

sections.md:
## What an exponent means
2⁵ means 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32. The 2 is the **base**; the 5 is the **exponent**, telling you how many times to multiply the base by itself.

## The rules
| Rule | Example | Why |
|---|---|---|
| aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ | x³ × x⁴ = x⁷ | 3 x's times 4 x's is 7 x's |
| aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ | x⁶ ÷ x² = x⁴ | Two x's cancel |
| (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ | (x²)³ = x⁶ | Three groups of two |
| a⁰ = 1 | 7⁰ = 1 | x³ ÷ x³ = 1 = x⁰ |
| a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ | 2⁻³ = 1/8 | Keep dividing by 2 |

sections.label: Common trap
sections.md: x² + x³ is **not** x⁵. The rules work for multiplying and dividing, not adding. You can't combine x² + x³ at all.

## Scientific notation
Write a number as (a number from 1 to just under 10) × (a power of 10).

- 5,800,000 = 5.8 × 10⁶ (move the decimal 6 places left)
- 0.00042 = 4.2 × 10⁻⁴ (move it 4 places right)

Big numbers get positive exponents; tiny numbers get negative ones.

practice.why: Anything (except 0) to the zero power is 1.
